Built inside a fire-safety company, not beside one

Safentia was commissioned by Firerite (UK) Limited, a fire-safety company. It did not begin as a product idea; it began as a working problem. Assessments were captured on paper, typed up in office software, and stitched into reports by hand. Photos lived in one place, floor plans in another, and the state of a job lived in somebody's head.

Safentia replaces that with one system. Assessors capture evidence on a native app, on site and offline. Auditors validate the work question by question. The report is generated from the assessment itself, not retyped from it. And every building keeps its history: RAG status, action plans, service schedules and an append-only log book.

One thing it is not: Safentia is software, not fire-safety consultancy. It helps the Responsible Person evidence a suitable and sufficient assessment under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005. The professional judgement, and the responsibility, stay where the law puts them.

safentia.co.uk/app

What the platform believes

Evidence over assertion

A finding is worth what stands behind it. Titled photos, floor-plan locations, named severities and an auditor's check turn a professional judgement into something the Responsible Person can rely on and a third party can verify.

The assessor's time on site is sacred

The visit is the expensive, unrepeatable part of an assessment. The app exists so that everything is captured once, properly, on the spot, and never reconstructed from memory at a desk two days later.

Reports the Responsible Person can act on

A report is not a deliverable to file; it is a list of decisions waiting to be made. Transparent question tables, a proportionally accurate risk profile and a severity-ordered action plan make the next step obvious.

The standards we align to

The Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005
The law that requires a suitable and sufficient assessment of fire risk, and places that duty on the Responsible Person.
PAS 79-1:2020
The publicly available specification setting out a methodology for fire risk assessment. Safentia's assessment structure follows it.
BS 9792
The British Standard covering fire risk assessment in housing, supported as a template alongside the PAS 79 structure.
